title: Kansas Faces Utah in Decisive Big 12 Showdown
seoTitle: Kansas Faces Undefeated Utah in Big 12 Showdown
subtitle: Jayhawks travel to Salt Lake City seeking a win against the undefeated Utes
excerpt: Kansas arrives in Utah after a 55-0 win over Middle Tennessee to face the undefeated 4-0 Utes in a matchup that promises to test both teams.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Following a 55-0 victory over Middle Tennessee, the Kansas Jayhawks head to Salt Lake City to face the Utah Utes, who enter the matchup with an undefeated start to the season (4-0). The game, scheduled for Saturday at 9:25 p.m. Central Time, is the first of eight consecutive Big 12 games for the Jayhawks.

Kansas head coach's expectations

Lance Leipold praised his team's attitude and work ethic, stating that while not everything is perfect, the squad is continually improving. The head coach believes the best football of the season is yet to come and will be essential against Utah.

Challenge of playing in a hostile environment

Defensive coordinator D.K. McDonald highlighted the need to keep players fresh and mentally motivated when facing an opponent that did Kansas no favors regarding travel. Rice-Eccles Stadium, known for its vibrant atmosphere, is expected to represent an additional obstacle for the visitors.

Utah's offensive profile

Utah features dual-threat quarterback Devon Dampier and running back Wayshawn Parker, both recognized as third-team All-Conference selections. The offense also incorporates large tight ends, such as Sione Motuapuaka and Semi Taulanga, who act as hybrid fullbacks, strengthening run blocking for Parker.

Kansas' new strategies

With the arrival of offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven, the Jayhawks adopted a scheme that, according to CBS Sports, creatively utilizes Dampier's backup, Byrd Ficklin, making it a nightmare for opposing defenses. Defensive coach McDonald acknowledges the creativity of McGiven's plan and praised its execution.

Areas for improvement

Despite the dominant win over Middle Tennessee, kickoff coverage showed vulnerabilities, as the opponent had two returns for more than 30 yards. Leipold attributed this to mistakes in positioning and player responsibility, pointing to the need for improvement ahead of the matchup against Utah.

Outlook for the matchup

Utah, which has allowed only 41 points through four games, presents a significant defensive challenge. On the other hand, Kansas seeks to regain its offensive rhythm, relying on the return of injured players and the development of Cam Pickett, who already demonstrated solid production against Middle Tennessee. The outcome will depend on both sides' ability to adapt their strategies and execute in a hostile environment.

With information from KU Sports.
